metaTitle: Best 20 Inch Lawn Mowers: Gas, Battery, Corded
metaDescription: Six 20 inch lawn mowers compared across gas, battery and corded power, with runtime, cutting height, self propel and storage explained for small lawns.
expertTake: The SKIL PWR CORE 40 self propelled 20 inch mower is the best all round choice: a brushless motor, up to 50 minutes from a 6.0 Ah pack and variable speed drive that makes slopes easy. The Greenworks 48V kit is the best push battery mower, and the CRAFTSMAN corded 13 amp mower is the value pick if an outlet is near your lawn. If you mow more than a third of an acre or very tall, wet grass weekly, skip 20 inch decks and look at a 21 or 22 inch self propelled gas mower.
introParagraphs: A 20 inch lawn mower is the compact size class for small to mid suburban lawns: narrow enough to store easily and push through gates, wide enough to finish a typical front and back yard in one session. Gas, battery and corded electric all come in this size, and their headline numbers are not directly comparable, which makes choosing harder than it looks.

This guide explains how engine displacement, battery voltage and amp hours, and motor amperage translate to cutting performance, why self propel matters on slopes, and what each power type costs you in upkeep. The quick picks are above, and the detailed reviews below match each mower to a lawn.

products.name: SKIL PWR CORE 40 20 in Self-Propelled Mower Kit, 6.0 Ah

specList.label: Battery
specList.value: PWR CORE 40 6.0 Ah, Auto PWR JUMP charger

products.description:
SKIL's self propelled 20 inch mower uses a 40V brushless motor for the blade and a separate drive system with variable speed, so the mower pulls itself at your walking pace. A 6.0 Ah PWR CORE 40 battery is rated for up to 50 minutes. Self propel matters most on slopes and when a bag is filling, which is when push mowers get heavy.

Against the SKIL push version, you get the drive system at the cost of weight and some runtime drain. The Craftsman V20 also claims up to 50 minutes with two 5 Ah packs, but has no self propel. For a quarter acre with gentle slopes, this is the most comfortable mower here.

The Auto PWR JUMP charger is designed to bring a pack to partial charge quickly, useful if you run out mid lawn. Sharpen the blade each season and clean grass from under the deck, since packed clippings increase motor load.
products.bestFor: Quarter acre lawns with slopes where a push mower gets tiring.
pros: Variable speed self propel makes slopes and full bags easy
Brushless motor holds blade speed in thick grass
Up to 50 minutes from the included 6.0 Ah pack
Push button start with no fuel or oil to handle
cons: Self propel adds weight and draws extra battery
PWR CORE 40 has fewer tools than the biggest platforms

products.name: Greenworks 48V (2 x 24V) 20 in Brushless Push Mower Kit
products.description:
Greenworks runs two 24V batteries in series to reach 48V, which gives the brushless motor more power while letting you keep the packs on the 24V platform for smaller tools. Two 4.0 Ah packs give up to 45 minutes. The 20 inch deck is steel, and the 3 year warranty covers the tool and batteries.

Compared with the SKIL self propelled at up to 50 minutes, you push it yourself, but you get a steel deck and a platform that shares batteries with Greenworks trimmers and blowers, including the 24V hedge trimmer. It suits flat to gently sloped lawns.

Steel decks resist cracking but can rust if grass is left caked on, so scrape the underside after wet mows. Store batteries indoors over winter.
products.bestFor: Flat lawns where a steel deck and shared 24V batteries are priorities.
pros: Two 24V packs combine for 48V without leaving the 24V line
Steel deck resists impacts and cracks
Brushless motor is efficient and quiet
3 year warranty includes the batteries
cons: No self propel, so slopes take effort
Steel deck needs cleaning to prevent rust

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 20 in Brushless Mower, 2 x 5.0 Ah

specList.label: Storage
specList.value: Folds vertical, takes 78% less floor space

products.description:
Craftsman's V20 mower runs a brushless motor on two 5.0 Ah V20 batteries and folds to stand vertically, taking much less garage floor space. Its low profile deck is about 10 inches tall at the lowest setting, which lets it reach under shrubs and benches. Runtime is rated up to 50 minutes.

Cut height runs 1.5 to 3.5 inches, narrower than the Craftsman corded mower's 1.5 to 4 inches, which matters if you keep a tall cut for heat tolerant grass. It shares batteries with the Craftsman hedge trimmer and hundreds of V20 tools.

Dual levers mean adjusting front and rear separately, so set both to the same notch. Clean the deck and keep the blade sharp to protect runtime.
products.bestFor: Small garages and V20 owners who need a compact mower.
pros: Folds upright to save floor space
Brushless motor with up to 50 minutes on two 5.0 Ah packs
Shares batteries with the big V20 tool line
Low deck reaches under shrubs
cons: 3.5 in maximum cut height is low for tall grass types
Dual lever height adjust is slower than single lever

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMEMW213 20 in Corded Mower, 13 Amp
products.description:
A 13 amp corded motor on a 120V outlet draws about 1,500 watts, more sustained power than many battery mowers deliver, and it never runs out of charge. The 20 inch deck supports mulching, bagging and side discharge, and a single lever sets cut height from 1.5 to 4 inches.

The tradeoff is the cord. You need a heavy outdoor extension cord, a GFCI protected outlet and a habit of mowing away from the cord. Against the battery mowers, it is the cheapest to buy and run, with no battery replacement after five or so years.

Use a 12 gauge cord for runs over about 50 feet to avoid voltage drop that overheats the motor. Keep the blade sharp and the deck clean.
products.bestFor: Small lawns near an outdoor outlet, on the lowest running cost.
pros: Unlimited runtime from a wall outlet
Single lever height adjust from 1.5 to 4 in
Mulch, bag and side discharge options
No batteries to replace years later
cons: Cord management around trees and beds is tedious
Needs a heavy gauge extension cord on longer runs

products.name: BILT HARD 20 in Gas Push Mower, 144cc OHV

specList.label: Wheels
specList.value: 7 in rear, 6 in front, ball bearing

products.description:
BILT HARD uses a 144cc overhead valve 4-stroke engine with an auto choke, so there is no primer bulb or choke lever to manage. OHV engines place valves in the cylinder head for better combustion and cooler running than older side valve designs. Single lever height adjust gives eight settings from 0.7 to 3.2 inches.

Compared with the SENIX at the same 144cc, the BILT HARD's auto choke and very low minimum height stand out; 0.7 inch suits warm season grasses like Bermuda kept short. Gas gives unlimited runtime with a quick refill, but adds oil changes and fuel upkeep.

Change the oil after the first 5 hours, then yearly. Use stabilized fuel and run the tank dry before winter.
products.bestFor: Gas buyers with short cut warm season lawns.
pros: Auto choke makes starting simple
Very low 0.7 in minimum cut height
OHV engine runs cleaner and cooler
Ball bearing wheels push easily
cons: Maximum 3.2 in cut is low for cool season grass
Oil, fuel and plug upkeep every season

products.name: SENIX 20 in 144cc Gas Push Mower, 3 in 1
products.description:
The SENIX is a basic 20 inch gas push mower with a 144cc 4-cycle engine and a 3 in 1 deck. Equal 7 inch wheels front and rear keep it simple and balanced. It is a lighter, compact gas mower for small lawns where you want fuel refills instead of charging.

It shares displacement with the BILT HARD, but without auto choke, so cold starts use a more traditional procedure. It also appears under a second listing; that is the same mower. Against the battery mowers, gas is louder and needs upkeep but never waits for a charge.

Check oil before every mow, since small push mower engines have little oil capacity. Clean the air filter and replace the plug each season.
products.bestFor: Budget gas buyers with small, flat lawns.
pros: Low cost gas mower with unlimited runtime
3 in 1 deck covers mulching and bagging
Compact size for small sheds
Simple engine with few electronics
cons: No auto choke, so cold starts take more steps
7 in wheels roll less easily on rough ground

buyingCriteria.explanation: Gas gives unlimited runtime but needs oil, fuel and plug upkeep. Battery mowers like the SKIL and Greenworks are quiet and simple but limited to 45 to 50 minutes per charge. Corded mowers like the CRAFTSMAN CMEMW213 are cheapest to run but tied to an outlet.

Voltage sets motor power and amp hours set runtime. Greenworks reaches 48V by pairing two 24V 4.0 Ah packs; SKIL uses a single 40V 6.0 Ah pack. Buy more amp hours if your lawn takes longer than about 40 minutes.

A self propelled drive takes the push effort away, which matters on slopes and with a full bag. The SKIL is the only self propelled 20 inch mower in this lineup. On flat lawns, a push mower is lighter and runs longer.

Cool season grasses like fescue do best around 3 to 4 inches, while warm season grasses are often cut much lower. The CRAFTSMAN corded reaches 4 inches, while the BILT HARD goes as low as 0.7 inch but only up to 3.2. Match the range to your grass.

Brushless motors on the SKIL, Greenworks and Craftsman V20 hold blade speed under load and waste less battery as heat. That is how they reach close to an hour of runtime. A brushless motor also has no brushes to wear.
Battery mowers can often fold and stand upright since there is no fuel or oil to spill. The Craftsman V20 claims 78 percent less floor space stored vertically. Gas mowers must stay level.

specDecoder.meaning: Cylinder volume of a gas engine. 144cc is typical for small push mowers.
specDecoder.watchFor: Displacement alone does not show torque; the BILT HARD lists 5.8 ft-lb, a more useful number when given.

specDecoder.meaning: Nominal battery voltage, which sets motor power potential.
specDecoder.watchFor: 48V on the Greenworks comes from two 24V packs in series; you need both charged to mow.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity; with voltage, sets stored energy and runtime.
specDecoder.watchFor: Runtime claims assume dry, short grass; thick or wet grass can cut runtime substantially.

specDecoder.meaning: Current draw of a corded motor; 13 amps at 120V is about 1,500 watts.
specDecoder.watchFor: A long thin extension cord drops voltage and makes the motor run hot and weak.

specDecoder.meaning: The deck can mulch, bag or side discharge clippings.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some 3 in 1 mowers need a separate plug or chute fitted; check what is in the box.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared engine displacement, battery voltage and motor type, plus corded amperage. Brushless motors scored well for holding blade speed. The SKIL and Greenworks led battery mowers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Runtime and refill
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed stated runtimes against lawn size. The SKIL and Craftsman V20 at up to 50 minutes led battery picks. Gas and corded mowers scored as unlimited with upkeep costs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at self propel, start method, height adjustment and weight. The SKIL's variable self propel and push button start ranked highest. Auto choke on the BILT HARD scored for gas.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut quality and range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared height ranges and deck options. The CRAFTSMAN corded's 1.5 to 4 inch range suits cool season grass. The BILT HARD's 0.7 inch minimum suits warm season grass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered warranties, platforms and maintenance needs. Greenworks' 3 year warranty including batteries and Craftsman's large network scored well. Gas mowers lost points for seasonal upkeep.

rows: Variable self propel on a brushless mower
Small lawn, gas on a budget
Auto choke and wide height range

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: Brushless motors, push button start, quiet operation and no fuel or oil. Runtime is capped by the pack. In this roundup: SKIL PWR CORE 40 Self-Propelled, Greenworks 48V and CRAFTSMAN V20.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: A 144cc 4-stroke engine with unlimited runtime and quick refills, at the cost of noise, oil changes and fuel storage. In this roundup: BILT HARD 20 in and SENIX 20 in.

howToChoose.note: For small lawns, battery is the easier ownership choice. Choose gas if you mow tall, wet grass often or need to mow longer than a battery lasts.

rows: Gas is fine away from living space

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Self propel with variable speed, enough runtime to finish without stopping, and good traction. Mow across slopes, not up and down, with walk behind mowers.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SKIL PWR CORE 40 Self-Propelled is the only self propelled 20 inch option here, with up to 50 minutes of runtime.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have slopes, a bigger lawn or already own a platform. The SKIL self propelled or Greenworks 48V kit pays back in comfort and battery reuse.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small and flat. The CRAFTSMAN corded mower or SENIX gas mower handles it for much less.

maintenance.why: A dull blade tears grass, leaving brown tips and stressing the lawn. It also makes the motor or engine work harder.
Packed wet clippings reduce airflow and cut quality. On steel decks, they also cause rust.
New engines shed metal particles early. Fresh oil protects bearings and the cylinder.
Stale fuel varnishes carburetor jets. Stabilizer or running dry prevents hard starts in spring.
Cold and heat shorten lithium life. Store at partial charge at room temperature.

faq.q: Is a 20 inch mower big enough for my lawn?
faq.a: It suits lawns up to roughly a quarter to a third of an acre. Larger lawns go faster with 21 or 22 inch decks or a riding mower.

faq.q: Battery or gas for a small lawn?
faq.a: Battery for most small lawns: quieter, no fuel and very little upkeep. Gas if you need unlimited runtime or mow tall wet grass often.

faq.q: How long do mower batteries last?
faq.a: Lithium packs typically last several years, depending on cycles and storage. Store them indoors at partial charge to extend life.

faq.q: Is a higher voltage mower always stronger?
faq.a: Not always. Motor design and blade matter, and brushless motors at 40V can match higher voltage brushed designs.

faq.q: What extension cord does a corded mower need?
faq.a: An outdoor rated cord plugged into a GFCI outlet. Use 14 gauge up to about 50 feet and 12 gauge beyond that to avoid voltage drop.

faq.q: Should I mulch or bag clippings?
faq.a: Mulching returns nutrients to the soil and is fine if you mow often. Bag when grass is very long or for a tidier finish.
